name: Luxaren
description: Luxaren is a sensory-enhancement compound that dramatically upregulates the thalamic relay systems responsible for processing visual and auditory input, making every sensation feel like the first time — colors achieve a depth and luminosity that sober perception cannot access, and music becomes a full-body architectural experience. It was developed as an accessibility drug to help individuals with sensory processing disorders, and its recreational popularity was entirely predictable.
effects: Extreme color saturation and depth perception enhancement
Music perceived as three-dimensional physical structures
Emotional resonance with art and sound
Mild euphoria and sense of wonder
side_effects: Sensory overload in loud or crowded environments
Occasional auditory hallucinations at high doses
Headache and eye strain during comedown
cultural_context: Luxaren is the drug of the creative class — musicians, visual artists, architects, and the people who love them. In Tier 2 and 3 entertainment districts, Luxaren nights are a recognized social institution: venues dim their lights, curate their sound systems, and sometimes offer Lux at the bar alongside alcohol. It's legal, it's relatively safe, and it's one of the few pleasures accessible to working-class people that genuinely feels elevated. The irony that Novafold prices the prescription form for sensory disorders at Φ 400 per dose while the street price is Φ 60 is not lost on anyone.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 musician has built an entire live performance around Luxaren — the show only makes complete sense to an audience on Lux, and she's being investigated for predatory drug-facilitated commerce
Someone is cutting street Luxaren with a compound that causes permanent thalamic sensitization — users come back reporting the effects never fully wore off, and not in a good way

A Tier 5 art collector is paying enormous sums to experience his private collection under curated pharmaceutical conditions — he wants a custom Luxaren blend tailored to a specific artist's palette, and he needs someone who knows the gray market
